newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Forint ends weaker vs dlr, seen staying below bid.
newsitem.headline: Forint ends weaker vs dlr, seen staying below bid.

text.p: The forint closed weaker against the dollar on Thursday and was seen keeping its distance from the central bank's resistence level (bid).
The Hungarian unit ended at 160.47/52, compared to an opening of 160.15/20, and stayed 50 pips from the bid.

"Today, the forint just followed a fluctuating dollar/mark cross on international markets," said Zsolt Tilimon of Citibank, adding that there were good reasons for the forint to stay below the central bank bid.
"The gap is not likely to change in the near future as there is more forex demand at the end of the year, when imports tend to be larger than exports," he said.
Tilimon added that maturing end-of-year futures contracts also increased demand for foreign currency on the spot market.
The currency section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange saw moderate turnover with most trade split between the dollar, Ecu and a large order in the March Swiss franc contract.
The dollar and yen mostly rose, the Ecu mostly fell, while the mark and sterling were mixed and the Swiss franc rose.
A new December 1997 contract for the lira opened at 121 forints for 1,000 lira.
